transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Hi, thanks. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I feel like I’m just constantly running on a motor lately. Like, I’ll finish one thing at school—I teach special ed, and let me tell you, the kids are great, but the administration right now is obsessed with these new IEP tracking forms. They changed the software three times this year. Three! I spent four hours on a Sunday just trying to figure out how to log a simple behavior incident for a kid who threw a stapler, and the IT guy, Dave, he never answers his emails. 

But anyway, yeah, it’s like I finish a task there, or even at home, and I just immediately jump right into the next thing without ever being able to shut myself off. I just keep going and going. I was supposed to be relaxing this weekend and ended up completely reorganizing the garage, which reminds me I still need to go to the hardware store to buy more of those clear plastic bins because the opaque ones make it impossible to find the holiday decorations... but yeah, I just can't seem to shut off.
Have you been sleeping less than usual lately?

Sleep? No, I don't think I'm sleeping any less than I usually do. I mean, I'm usually in bed around the same time, though lately I've been trying out this new memory foam pillow. You know the ones that are supposed to have that blue cooling gel inside them? I saw an infomercial for it when I was up late grading those IEPs I mentioned earlier. The guy on the TV was talking about how it aligns your cervical spine, and I thought, well, at my age, my neck isn't exactly what it used to be. 

Especially since I'm always leaning over those tiny desks in the classroom. You'd think they would make the furniture adjustable for the teachers, right? Like, I'm a grown man, and I'm bending completely in half to help a kid with a fraction worksheet, and my lumbar is just screaming by 2 PM. My chiropractor—Dr. Evans, great guy, he actually does close-up magic tricks in the waiting room—he told me I need to do more core exercises. Like planks. But honestly, who wants to do a plank? A minute feels like a whole year when you're doing a plank. 

Anyway... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, sleeping less. No, no, my actual hours of sleep are about the same as always. I just wake up and I'm immediately at a hundred miles an hour again.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, irritable, or overly confident lately?

High or overly confident? No, no, definitely not confident. I mean, how can anyone be overly confident these days? Especially at work with that new software. I'm just trying to keep my head above water! But my mood itself is fine. 

I wouldn't say I'm unusually irritable either... well, unless you count dealing with my brother-in-law, Gary. We had him and my sister over for dinner on Thursday. I made a brisket, actually. Smoked it for 12 hours out back on the patio. You really have to keep a close eye on the wood chips—I usually mix hickory and applewood because the applewood gives it this really nice, sweet finish, but you can't let it burn too hot or it completely dries out the meat. You want it to just fall apart when you cut it. 

Anyway, Gary just chewed my ear off about his cryptocurrency investments the entire time we were eating. I swear the guy thinks he's the next Warren Buffett. It just sounds like fake internet money to me, and I told him that, which maybe was a little blunt, but I just don't have the patience for it. Plus he kept letting the screen door slam every time he went out to the deck, and we just got that fixed because the dog kept scratching at the mesh... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, my mood. Right. No, no unusual highs or anything like that. Just my normal self, really.
Have you been feeling more anxious or worried lately, even when there isn't a clear reason for it?

Anxious? Worried? No, not really. I mean, I don't sit around worrying about things out of the blue. If I'm stressed, it's usually because of something specific, like those IEP forms I was telling you about. But just general anxiety? No. 

Though, you know, speaking of worrying, my wife has been on this huge kick lately about our water quality. She read some article online—probably on Facebook, honestly, she spends half her evening scrolling through those community groups. You wouldn't believe the drama in our neighborhood association. Last week, Mrs. Higgins from down the street tried to pass a rule about what color you're allowed to paint your mailbox. Can you imagine? A mailbox! Who cares if it's beige or eggshell? 

But anyway, my wife read this thing about hard water and minerals, and now she wants us to install this massive water filtration system for the whole house. I looked at the manual for it, and it's like an airplane engine. It has all these reverse osmosis filters and carbon tanks, and you have to change them out every six months, which you know I'll be the one doing. I already have to change the furnace filters, and the ones I buy are those pleated ones that catch pet dander, because of the dog. He's a golden retriever mix, sheds like you wouldn't believe. I have to vacuum the living room rug twice a week just to keep it from looking like a shag carpet. 

But... wait. Anxiety. Right. No, no, I don't feel anxious for no reason. I just have a lot to do, you know? But no unusual worrying.
